messages:
Maya (Marketing): sprint brief  goal: a compact battlecard that contrasts our 'serving-first' stance vs cloud API vendors and DIY inference. keep it <1 page and rep-ready.
Noor (PMM): focus on migration risk reduction and ops guarantees. buyers want escape hatches, not vendor romance.
Sam (Sales): reps ask for: 1) 15s opener 2) 30s discovery + 1 pricing rebuttal. also two quick zingers vs clouds.
Priya (Research): bench headline we'll cite: embedding pipelines saw ~28-35% unit-cost drop with our batching+quantization profile; p95 tail stayed within SLA. I'll provide a 1-paragraph methods blurb.
Owen (Field): ops checklist to include: reserved capacity options, KMS + HSM integrations, private VPC deploy, audit log retention, and exportable traces. procurement likes explicit exit steps.
Ravi (Content): I'll layout a 1-pager and a 3-slide "migration play": slide1=why risk matters, slide2=how we mitigate, slide3=rep scripts + FAQ.
Maya (Marketing): webinar idea: 20-min customer story (anonymized) + 30-min runbook (live demo of fallback & rollback) + 10-min Q&A. webinar-bot, can we grab a provisional slot?
webinar-bot: Provisional hold created: 2024-08-22 11:00 UTC  calendar hold.
Sam (Sales): draft sales lines: 
- 15s opener: "Do you get surprised by inference bills or tail latency? Redwood makes serving predictable and auditable."
- 30s discovery: "When you push models to prod, do you have guardrails to keep latency and unit cost steady? We give reserved capacity, verified runtime optimizations, and rapid rollback paths so migrations don't become crises."
Priya (Research): add quality guard: "We bind batching/quantization changes to prompt-linked evals and regression alerts so quality doesn't slip under savings."
Noor (PMM): competitor zingers (short):
- vs cloud APIs: "They scale models; we stabilize bill and behavior in production."
- vs DIY infra: "Skip fragile glue code: verified runtime + control plane = deploy-safe inference."
Owen (Field): I'll draft a procurement FAQ covering SLA language, exit/export mechanics, and a short note on compliance.
Maya (Marketing): deliverables & owners: 1-pager + 3-slide migration play (Ravi), rep scripts + zingers (Sam), bench methods + numbers (Priya), procurement FAQ + case stub (Owen), final assembly + landing copy (Maya). lock in 5 business days.
Ravi (Content): putting templates in the draft folder: https://drive.redwood.example/marketing/battlecards/serving-first-draft :pushpin:
Sam (Sales): I'll also add two quick objection handlers for: pricing variability, vendor lock-in.
Priya (Research): posting the methods blurb + small table in the drive in ~90m. will include the exact cache/batch/quant knobs.
Maya (Marketing): awesome. if legal clears the anonymized story, we use it as the webinar hook headline: "A painless migration: 30% lower spend, no quality regression." otherwise use a composite case. reopen thread if blockers. :rocket:
